name: veterinary_clinic_system_046_appointment_reminder_queue_fill
instruction: Refill the appointment-reminder queue for the next 7 days, batched under the episode batch code. The eligible window is appointment_date between episode_date + 1 day and episode_date + 7 days inclusive, status 'scheduled' or 'confirmed'. For each eligible appointment whose patient does not already appear in any queued reminder_queue row (any kind) as of the start of the run, push one reminder_queue row: kind 'appointment_reminder', patient_id, owner_id (from the patient record), due_date set to the appointment's date, message 'Appointment reminder: <PatientName> on <YYYY-MM-DD> at <start_time>.', status 'queued', queued_by 'system', queued_at the episode timestamp, batch_code, channel copied from the active reminder_templates row whose trigger is 'appointment_reminder' (the template is a real appointment-reminder template; do not hardcode the channel), and priority 'high' if the appointment reason contains any of the urgent keywords 'vomit', 'limping', 'lameness', or 'ear infection' (case-insensitive), otherwise 'normal'. Patients who already have any queued reminder of any kind (e.g., vaccination_due or boarding_checkin) must be skipped entirely. Delete any existing appointment_reminder rows for this batch before pushing new ones; all other reminder_queue rows must remain untouched.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps must be measured against a live container in the QC session; do not set final values without a real gold run.

success_criteria.summary: One new appointment_reminder row per eligible appointment whose patient has no pre-existing queued reminder. Exact fields (message, due_date, channel, priority, batch_code) verified per row. Seeded reminder_queue rows byte-identical. Counts and priority totals recomputed by raw-row Python filter and independent SQL and must agree.

checks.expect: exact per-row match of new appointment_reminder rows keyed by patient_id+due_date, seeded rows unchanged
total eligible count, per-priority counts, and excluded-patient counts agree between raw-row filter and SQL

hazards: Existing queued reminder_queue patients are decoys: row id 1 (patient 2, vaccination_due, queued), id 2 (patient 5, vaccination_due, queued), id 4 (patient 8, boarding_checkin, queued). For episode dates around 2026-09-27, those patients also have upcoming appointments in the 7-day window (patient 5 has appointment id 400 on 2026-09-29; patient 8 has appointment id 543 on 2026-09-30). A solution that does not check the live queued state will produce duplicate reminders.

Same-day (episode date) scheduled/confirmed appointments must not receive a next-day reminder. For episode 2026-09-30, examples include id 69 (confirmed, Dental prophylaxis consult), id 112 (confirmed, Skin allergy flare-up), and id 125 (scheduled, Vomiting since yesterday) — all on 2026-09-30. An off-by-one date filter (>= episode date instead of > episode date) will queue them.

Stale scheduled/confirmed appointments with dates before the episode date are not eligible. Example: id 74 (scheduled, Ear infection re-check, 2026-09-27) is before episode 2026-09-30 but remains in 'scheduled' status; a solution without the lower date bound may queue it.
The active appointment_reminder template has trigger 'appointment_reminder' and channel 'sms' (reminder_templates id 5). A hardcoded channel 'email' or using the first template will fail.

Priority classification is by keyword, not by appointment priority field. 'Vaccine boosters due' (routine) and 'Vomiting since yesterday' (urgent) can look similar in length; an agent that matches 'vaccine' inside 'vomiting' or vice versa will misclassify. 'Annual wellness exam' is routine, 'Ear infection re-check' is urgent, and 'Chronic kidney disease monitoring' is standard.

Idempotency: a second run must delete the batch's own appointment_reminder rows (identified by kind + batch_code) before rewriting; otherwise the second run would double the queue and the skip-patient logic would exclude legitimate rows.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Combines a multi-day reminder fill with live queue de-duplication, channel lookup from a template, reason-based urgency classification, and batch-keyed idempotency. The verifier uses dual-path appointment counts and per-row priority/channel checks at 10x appointment volume. No public benchmark combines these three concerns (queue fill + template-driven channel + triage priority) in one task.
